BACKGROUND. The hosted @llm-canon test (the second big test in scene-runtime.spec.js, titled 'judges every reached scene against its committed knowledge canon @llm-canon') walks the nine-scene continuity_initiative story with a fixed script and then judges each scene. Three real runs aborted on harness mistakes, not game faults. This task fixes the harness only. Read the test body first (roughly lines 219-420) and the helpers in /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/frontend/e2e/package-clock.js (loadPackagePacing, canonTurnBudget, nextPendingEvent; the pacing projection has sceneOrder, eventOrder, scenePoint, eventPoint, isConditional). Mirror the style of package-clock.test.js for tests.

CHANGE F1 - delete the false stall gate. Remove the constant `MAX_STALLED_TURNS` (with its comment), the `let stalledTurns = 0; let lastCommittedCount = 0;` declarations, and the whole block that computes `committed`, updates stalledTurns/lastCommittedCount and ends with `.toBeLessThan(MAX_STALLED_TURNS)`. Add no replacement and no new progress metric. Keep the canonTurnBudget loop bound as is.

CHANGE F3 - require a pacing event only when play actually reached its due turn in its own scene. Today the per-turn loop over pacing.eventOrder treats every event of any scene already left as overdue, so a scene left early (the 1C incident route completes the scene in 3 turns) falsely fails on an unconditional event whose target turn (e.g. transfer_window_1c at 5) was never reached. Put the policy in a new pure module canon-policy.js exporting `requiredPacingEvents({ pacing, sourceSceneId, reachedSceneId, observedTurns, turnsSinceSceneEntry })` that returns the array of event ids (in pacing.eventOrder order) that this turn requires, where an event is required when EITHER (a) event.scene_id === reachedSceneId && observedTurns >= event.target_turn (still in its scene, past due), OR (b) event.scene_id === sourceSceneId && reachedSceneId !== sourceSceneId && turnsSinceSceneEntry + 1 >= event.target_turn (the player left the scene on the very turn the event was due; turnsSinceSceneEntry is the counter BEFORE the turn, and the +1 is the one accepted turn just taken). An event of the source scene that is not yet due at departure is NOT required, and the destination scene's counter must never be compared with a source-scene event. Then in the spec replace the old comment and the `eventScene`/`inScenePastDue` lines with a call to this helper: `for (const eventId of requiredPacingEvents({...}))` followed by the existing conditional skip (pacing.isConditional(eventId) and not in payload.state?.fired_pacing_event_ids -> continue, keep its comment), the existing expect(...).toContain(eventId), and firedPacingEventIds.add(eventId). Keep ALSO adding to firedPacingEventIds any event id present in payload.state?.fired_pacing_event_ids that the clock may steer toward (do not break the existing behaviour that a fired conditional event is recorded). Import the helper at the top next to the package-clock import.

CHANGE F4 - finish the story before judging. Replace the loop line `if (sceneId === sceneOrder.at(-1) && (promptsUsed.get(sceneId) || 0) >= scenePrompts[sceneId].length) break;` with exactly `if (storyCompleteSeen) break;`. Immediately after the existing line `expect(sceneId, "the playthrough must end in the authored resolution scene").toBe(sceneOrder.at(-1));` add `expect(storyCompleteSeen, "the story must actually complete; reaching 3C is not the ending").toBe(true);` so the nine judge calls never run for a journey that exhausted its budget without completing. If `scenePrompts` becomes unused in the spec after this, drop it from the import. The prompt cycling (promptFor uses modulo) already supplies prompts past the end of a scene's list; do not change canon-journey.js.

TESTS in canon-policy.test.js (node:test, assert/strict), using a small hand-built fake pacing object (sceneOrder, eventOrder, eventPoint(id)) so no real package is needed, PLUS at least one test on the real continuity_initiative package loaded as in package-clock.test.js: (1) scene left early at relative turn 3 with an unconditional event at 5 in the left scene -> NOT required; (2) still in the scene at observed turn 5 with that event unfired -> required; (3) departing exactly when turnsSinceSceneEntry + 1 === target_turn -> required, and one turn earlier -> not required; (4) an event of a scene after the reached scene is never required; (5) an event of an earlier scene than the source (already handled on previous turns) is never required again; (6) the destination counter being 0 after a transition does not require or hide anything for the source scene's events; (7) on the real package, the 1C early-exit case (sourceSceneId '1C', reachedSceneId '2A', turnsSinceSceneEntry 2) does not require transfer_window_1c. Work out each expectation from the data/stories/continuity-initiative/pacing.yaml and from the rule above before asserting it, and keep assertions to cases you verified by running the tests.

Style: match the surrounding files; no unrelated refactors; do not touch the test titled for @llm-canon beyond the three changes above.

BACKGROUND. scene-walk.js walks the story scene by scene for judge probes. It has two defects shared with the canon spec: (1) a false stall gate - `MAX_STALLED_TURNS = 5`, the `stalled`/`committed` variables and the block after `onTurn` that throws `Scene X stalled for N turns` when the count of payload.state.fired_storylet_ids stops growing. A scene legitimately goes many turns without a new reveal while its pacing events (patrol arrival/departure, search pressure) advance, so the gate aborts good runs. (2) Its local `milestoneFor` picks its own pending pacing event with `candidate.target_turn >= turns` for every event, so an unfired CONDITIONAL event (one whose pacing `when` is non-empty) keeps being the armed target on its own turn and the turn after overshoots it. frontend/e2e/package-clock.js already exports `nextPendingEvent(pacing, sceneId, currentTurns, firedEventIds)` which fixes this (conditional events are targets only while strictly ahead). Read package-clock.js first.

CHANGE F1. Delete `const MAX_STALLED_TURNS = 5;`, the `let stalled = 0; let committed = 0;` lines, and the four lines computing committedNow / stalled / committed and throwing the stall error. Add nothing in their place. Keep the existing maxTurns limit (`Scene walk exceeded its N-turn limit.`) and the handoff error in milestoneFor - those remain the bounds.

CHANGE F2. Add `import { nextPendingEvent } from "./package-clock.js";` under the existing import, and in milestoneFor replace the local `const event = (pacing.eventOrder || []).map(...).find(...)` with `const event = nextPendingEvent(pacing, sceneId, turns, fired);` (keep `if (event) return event;`). Do not add duck-typing fallbacks in production code: fake pacing objects in tests must implement the projection's real contract.

TESTS in scene-walk.test.js. The existing test `reports a stall rather than spending the turn budget` enshrines the removed behaviour: replace it with (a) a test that a run which never reaches its target scene fails with the bounded terminal error (/exceeded its \d+-turn limit/) after maxTurns, and (b) a test with a reveal-free interval: six or more consecutive responses in scene 1A with fired_storylet_ids unchanged (committed constant) followed by a response entering 1B must now succeed (no stall error) and report the right opening for 1B. Complete the shared fake `pacing` object with `isConditional() { return false; }` and `eventPoint(id)` as needed so nextPendingEvent works with it (nextPendingEvent reads pacing.eventOrder, eventPoint and isConditional; read how it uses them). Add tests that observe the ACTUAL armed target by passing a fake controller whose `arm(milestone)` records its argument: (c) a conditional event that stays unfired at and after its due turn is armed only while strictly ahead, then the walker falls back to the next scene point; (d) an unconditional event due at the current turn is still armed; (e) a fired event (fired_pacing_event_ids in the response state) is no longer armed. Work out each expectation from the code before asserting, and keep assertions to cases you verified by running the tests. Style: match the file; no unrelated refactors.
